name: pulse-fast
concept: The element snaps to a much larger scale and back, very fast and continuous. Reserve it for the single most urgent item on a screen, like a critical status badge.

name: pulse-overshoot
concept: The element grows past its target size, then settles back slightly before the loop repeats. A springy, elastic way to say this moved for a reason.

name: pulse-anticipate
concept: The element dips smaller first, then grows large before returning to rest. The wind-up reads as gathering energy before the emphasis lands.

name: pulse-strobe-scale
concept: The element pops twice in tight, back-to-back succession with almost no rest between beats. Reads as stark and mechanical, more clipped than a normal fast pulse.

name: pulse-fade
concept: The element grows and dims at the same time, then returns to rest, continuous. A wavering way to keep drawing the eye without a hard flash.

name: pulse-flash-scale
concept: The element pops larger while dropping sharply in opacity, then recovers, continuous. Near-flash urgency, but the scale change sets it apart from a plain flash.

name: pulse-warning
concept: The element dims sharply while growing only a little, fast and continuous. Reads as a caution or hazard cue rather than a simple highlight.

name: pulse-flicker
concept: The element flickers twice with a small twitch of scale, then holds steady until the loop restarts. Reads as an unstable signal rather than a steady pulse.

name: pulse-ghost
concept: The element shrinks and fades instead of growing, then returns, continuous. A receding pulse that still draws the eye, just by contrast rather than by getting bigger.

name: throb-snap
concept: The element expands quickly, then eases back down slowly, continuous. An asymmetric throb that reads as a sudden swell with a soft release.

name: throb-linger
concept: The element builds up slowly, then snaps back down fast, continuous. The mirror image of throb-snap: patient growth, sudden release.

name: throb-hold
concept: The element grows quickly, holds at its peak size for a moment, then contracts, continuous. The pause at full size sets it apart from a simple asymmetric throb.

name: throb-heavy
concept: The element builds slowly to a large peak size, then releases fast, continuous. The big amplitude and long build make it feel weighty and deliberate.

name: glow-ring
concept: A ring built from box-shadow blooms outward from the element's edge and fades, continuous. A solid, elastic-feeling halo, distinct from a blurred filter glow.

name: pulse-double
concept: The element pulses twice in quick succession, then pauses before the loop repeats. Reads as a double-tap notification rather than one steady beat.

name: pulse-triple
concept: The element pulses three times in rapid succession, then pauses before the loop repeats. More insistent than a double pulse, without becoming a strobe.

name: pulse-heartbeat
concept: The element beats once strongly, then once more softly, then pauses, continuous. Mimics a heartbeat's lub-dub rhythm for a living, vital-sign feel.

name: pulse-double-fade
concept: The element pulses twice, each beat dipping in opacity as well as size, then pauses. A more urgent cousin of a plain double pulse.

name: glow-build
concept: A halo brightens gradually over several seconds, then resets sharply to nothing, continuous. Reads as something charging up rather than idly glowing.

name: glow-fuse
concept: Light gathers slowly at first, then accelerates into a bright flare before cutting out, continuous. Use it for a countdown or a rare, escalating cue.

name: glow-charge
phrase: glow and hold at full charge
concept: Brightness climbs steadily, holds at full intensity for a moment, then cuts back to nothing, continuous. Like a battery reaching full charge before it resets.

name: pulse-corner-tl
concept: The element grows from its top-left corner instead of its center, continuous. Suited to a badge or icon that is visually anchored to that corner.

name: pulse-corner-tr
concept: The element grows from its top-right corner instead of its center, continuous. Suited to a badge or icon that is visually anchored to that corner.

name: pulse-corner-bl
concept: The element grows from its bottom-left corner instead of its center, continuous. Suited to a badge or icon that is visually anchored to that corner.

name: pulse-corner-br
concept: The element grows from its bottom-right corner instead of its center, continuous. Suited to a badge or icon that is visually anchored to that corner.

name: pulse-edge-top
concept: The element grows from its top edge instead of its center, continuous. Suited to an element docked to the top of a bar or a panel.

name: pulse-edge-bottom
concept: The element grows from its bottom edge instead of its center, continuous. Suited to an element docked to the bottom of a bar or a panel.

name: pulse-edge-left
concept: The element grows from its left edge instead of its center, continuous. Suited to an element docked to the left side of a bar or a panel.

name: pulse-edge-right
concept: The element grows from its right edge instead of its center, continuous. Suited to an element docked to the right side of a bar or a panel.

name: glow-brighten
concept: Brightness itself pulses up and down rhythmically, continuous. Like a light source getting brighter and dimmer, without any change in size.

name: glow-saturate
concept: Color saturation intensifies and calms rhythmically, continuous. Makes an element's own color read as more alive, without moving or resizing it.

name: glow-deep
concept: A large, heavily blurred halo blooms slowly and recedes, continuous. A diffuse glow for elements that should feel important but calm.

name: glow-tight
concept: A small, tightly focused glow blips on and off twice in quick succession, continuous. A crisp, minimal cue rather than a soft halo.

name: glow-layered
concept: Two glows of different sizes bloom together, a tight inner glow and a wide outer one, continuous. Gives the halo more depth than a single blur.

name: glow-contrast
concept: Contrast punches up and back rhythmically, continuous. Makes the element look momentarily punchier and more defined, without moving or resizing.

name: glow-pulse-sync
concept: The element grows and glows at exactly the same moment, continuous. Size and light reinforce the same beat instead of competing for attention.

name: glow-pulse-offset
phrase: pulse and glow out of step
concept: Size and glow move out of step with each other, the halo peaking while the element is actually smallest, continuous. A layered, more complex read than a synced pulse.

name: pulse-corner-glow
phrase: pulse and glow from a corner
concept: The element grows from a corner while glowing, continuous. Suited to a badge or icon docked at an edge that needs both a size cue and a glow.

name: throb-glow
concept: An asymmetric throb, quick to grow and glow, slow to settle back down, continuous. Combines the urgency of a fast swell with the warmth of light.

name: pulse-urgent-triple-flash
concept: Three fast scale-and-opacity flashes fire in a row, then a longer pause, continuous. The most insistent motion in the set, for something that cannot be missed.

name: pulse-squash
concept: The element squashes wide and flat at its peak instead of growing evenly, continuous. A springy, cartoon-like way to draw the eye.

name: pulse-stretch-vertical
concept: The element stretches tall and narrow at its peak, continuous. Reads as reaching upward, good for a vertical list item or a column highlight.

name: pulse-stretch-horizontal
concept: The element stretches wide and short at its peak, continuous. Reads as spreading sideways, good for a row or a horizontal bar highlight.

name: pulse-diagonal-corner
phrase: pulse and lean from a corner
concept: The element grows from a corner while nudging slightly along the diagonal toward the center, continuous. A corner pulse with a faint sense of reaching inward.

name: pulse-fade-deep
concept: A slow, smooth pulse where opacity drops almost to nothing at the peak while size barely changes, continuous. A deep, moody fade rather than a sharp flash.

name: glow-pulse-warning
concept: A fast, urgent glow blip pairs with a small scale pop, continuous. Reads as an alert light rather than an ambient halo.

name: pulse-quick-release-corner
concept: An asymmetric throb anchored at a corner, quick to expand and slow to settle, continuous. For a corner badge that needs urgency rather than a gentle pulse.

name: pulse-slow-build-scale
concept: The element creeps larger over several seconds, then snaps back to rest and starts again, continuous. A slow-building size cue that mirrors a building glow, through scale instead of light.

name: pulse-double-corner
concept: Two quick pulses anchored at a corner, then a pause, continuous. Combines the double-beat rhythm with a fixed anchor point for a docked element.

name: throb-whisper
concept: A very low-amplitude asymmetric throb, quick to rise and slow to settle, continuous. The quietest option in the set, for something that should stay noticeable without shouting.
